Example scenarios

Question to verify

Does the recipient understand what they are buying?

The same service, price, and scope. We compare how value is presented.

A / From features

“CRM, automations, and integrations with company systems.”

B / From the company's situation

“Enquiry, quote, and next contact in one place. The team sees who is handling the enquiry.”

Questions from three perspectives
Business owner

What result is the contractor responsible for?

Operations specialist

What will change in the current process?

Future user

Do I know what to do after receiving an enquiry?

What we prepare

Unclear parts of the offer, recurring objections, and suggested changes.

Next test

We discuss the revised offer with real recipients.

Question to verify

Does the message address a key problem?

The same invoice workflow. We compare two starting points for conversation.

A / From tool capabilities

“Reading invoice data and suggesting a document classification.”

B / From daily work

“Invoice data is sent for review. Differences in amounts are highlighted before approval.”

Questions from three perspectives
Business owner

What business problem does this solve?

Operations specialist

Who will check exceptions and incorrect data?

Future user

Do I understand how the system will help me today?

What we prepare

Differences in message comprehension and the questions the text should answer.

Next test

We select variants for discussions or testing on live traffic.

Question to verify

Where is accountability missing in the new process?

The same stage of enquiry handling. We compare how work is handed over to a human.

A / Summary only

“AI describes the enquiry and shows it to the team.”

B / Summary with a next step

“AI highlights missing information and suggests an action. The enquiry owner reviews the suggestion and decides.”

Questions from three perspectives
Business owner

Who is responsible for the decision and its outcome?

Operations specialist

What happens when data is missing?

Future user

Do I know what I am approving and how to adjust the proposal?

What we prepare

Work handover points, missing rules, and situations requiring a human decision.

Next test

We review the workflow with the team on a single real-world example.

Our context. Our working method.

What we develop in-house

We develop Matrix for specific business decisions. We combine custom scenarios with audience profiles, model response comparison, and experiment quality control.

Scenarios and profiles
Company offering, B2B pricing, website copy, or a new process. We tailor context and roles to the question.
Comparison of variants
We examine rationales, objections, and differences between models. Mere agreement between responses is not enough.
Quality control
We alter the order of responses and how questions are asked. We look for repeatable errors and unstable conclusions.
Material for decision-making
We organize observations, highlight limitations, and select hypotheses to test in the actual process.

Simulations help prepare a better test. We verify their outcome with humans — it is not a sales forecast or market research.

Technology: we develop Matrix based on the open-source project MatrAIx , with our own layer of scenarios, analysis, and quality control. Authorship of the source project belongs to its creators.

02 / Our own work system

bOS.
From agreed details to execution.

We develop bOS so that working with AI has context, continuity, and a result that can be verified.

Models work with source material

The starting point is project files, agreed details, code, and sources. bOS helps find context, organize the task, and prepare an analysis or change. The result can be a working feature, a report, documentation, or material for further work.

A second opinion on the same brief

When we need additional verification, our ICC bridge allows us to compare responses from different models. We review evidence, discrepancies, and counterarguments. We remain responsible for evaluating the result and for the work we deliver.

From our work / Council development, August 2026bOS helps
build bOS.

We improved our own AI Council. A trial on real models revealed a flaw: a matching response could be presented as proof.

This is what the path from idea through code to verifying whether the change actually works looks like.

01Independent models, one task+

We expanded the Council with peer review and a joint summary. In the trial, Claude and Grok first answered separately, then evaluated each other's arguments. Gemini prepared a synthesis. The task lead compared the result with the sources.

Two independent opinions, two reviews, and a synthesis were completed.
02Trial reveals a weak point+

In the summary, the model was capable of calling the other models' consensus "confirmed evidence". It sounded convincing, but did not indicate the source or the test result. This case showed what needed to be improved in the Council itself.

A completed discussion is not enough to validate a conclusion.
03Fix and retest+

We refined the requirements: confirmed evidence must indicate a source or a reproducible result. The report separately shows the execution of stages and the need for verification. In a subsequent run without evidentiary material, the model correctly reported a lack of confirmed evidence.

The task lead remains responsible for checking the result.
04We also check refusal+

23 tests verified the Council mechanism. The attempt with a single provider was rejected; input with a test secret pattern was as well. What remains is the code, tests, and reports that can be revisited with the next change.

Result of this stage: a locally working mechanism and saved verification records.
On the computer, in apps, and via API

In daily work, bOS connects code, documents, and connected tools. We use APIs and MCP connections; an agent can also operate a browser on our computer, complete a form, and inspect the result.

For an earlier version of the ISIKO website, we verified the actual views and button functionality in the browser. After publishing, we separately retrieved the active version via the Cloudflare API and compared the public files with the prepared release.

Separate security review

We also include Daybreak in code reviews. We check reported issues in the source code and attempt to reproduce them. The model's opinion is evaluated alongside test results.

We define the scope of access and actions for each task. Permissions in client systems are controlled by code, and we carry out publishing or system changes within the agreed scope. We develop bOS and work on client systems in the exact same way.

Discover Dopina solutions

04 / Research direction

AI in the physical world.

We are interested in the relationship between observing the environment, predicting the effects of actions, and motion planning.

We track the development of models that combine vision, language, and action. We analyze how they compare expected outcomes with what actually occurred, and adjust their next step accordingly.

This is the research direction of VARDE Labs. In our services, we focus on concrete AI implementations in processes, documents, and team workflows.
